title: Q3 Roadmap Launch Readiness - Product & Eng Sync
summary: Internal sync to align Product and Engineering on Q3 launch readiness items: finalize rollout checklist, confirm load test windows and owners, follow up on incident postmortem actions, and unblock documentation/runbook ownership. Decisions: push a small set of low-risk integrations to post-launch, prioritize SLOs and SRE-run load tests this week.
transcript:
Header: Q3 Roadmap Launch Readiness - Product & Eng Sync
Date/Time: 2026-07-15 10:00 AM PDT | Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Ravi, Elena, Connor, Priya
Shared artifacts: Q3 launch checklist (docs.redwood.link/q3-checklist), perf plan spreadsheet (sheets.redwood.link/perf-q3), incident postmortem (docs.redwood.link/pm-incident)

[00:00] Maya: okay uh let's get started, thanks everyone for coming, I know this is a packed week so we'll try to keep to the checklist. I put the Q3 launch readiness doc in the chat, link again after.

[00:22] Ravi: yeah thanks, I skimmed it, looks good. main things i want to confirm are the load test windows and the KV cash—sorry kv cache warmup steps, and the canary rollback criteria.

[00:40] Elena: kv cache, haha, i totally read cash first too. on the warmup we need roughly 10 minutes of prefix fill per instance type to avoid cold-start thumps. that's for the Dedicated pools and the private deploys. for hosted we can use faster prefix sampling.

[01:10] Connor: on the SRE side, we've got a tentative slot next wed night for scale test, but we need sign-off on the exact RPS and sequence length distribution. current perf plan sheet shows a 60k tokens/sec target which might be optimistic for 8xA100 mix.

[01:38] Maya: right, agree let's be conservative. Priya, can you confirm the customer-facing SLA we want to promise for GA? i remember product leaning on a 99.9 latency SLO for p95 on simple generation calls?

[01:55] Priya: we should not overpromise. product preference is 99.9 uptime and p95 latency under 250ms for short prompts, but engineering recommended targeting p95 under 350ms for GA and tighten post-GA. so decision pending.

[02:20] Ravi: SLOs are fine, but call out that p95 depends a lot on batching and caching. if customers enable aggressive batching or have long seq lengths that will blow the p95. we should add guidance to the docs: recommended batching config by workload.

[02:45] Elena: yes, add the quantization profile note too; for some open models we saw a 1.8x throughput improvement but a slight quality delta. need a short blurb in the checklist about QA for quantized variants.

[03:10] Maya: good. incident postmortem follow-ups — Connor you were leading one of the items, what's the status on autop-runbook for the circuit-breaker we tripped in June?

[03:28] Connor: partial. i pushed the initial alert rule changes and the tracing hook, but the automated mitigation script still needs the safety check for fallback model variant. that's the blocker. i estimate another 3 dev days.

[03:50] Ravi: is that blocking the launch? not necessarily, as long as the manual runbook steps are clean and the on-call knows the play. but we need the automation before we go full GA on Dedicated.

[04:10] Maya: okay action: Connor to finish the mitigation script and add test cases. Priya can own the runbook doc updates so the on-call has a clear checklist.

[04:28] Priya: noted, i will update the runbook and schedule a dry-run with on-call next tuesday.

[04:45] Speaker 6 (off): quickly, on launch messaging, do we list Dedicated and Private as GA simultaneously?

[04:58] Maya: we discussed rolling GA: hosted API GA first, then Dedicated in a phased way, Private follows with customer-by-customer on-prem checks. we'll be explicit in the release notes.

[05:20] Elena: on the perf tests, one thing to call out: our kernel selection code sometimes picks slower kernel for specific sequence lengths, need a guard to prefer the quantized kernel when throughput wins. that's an engineering TODO but impacts the load test configurations.

[05:45] Ravi: good catch. add to perf plan sheet with example sequence bins.

[06:03] Maya: alright let's walk the checklist items one by one. item one: final feature lock — are there any last-minute feature toggles we need to move to post-launch?

[06:20] Elena: the embeddings rerank integration is still in progress; i suggest we cut that to post-launch. it's low-usage but high risk.

[06:35] Priya: agreed, move embeddings rerank to post-launch. update the checklist.

[06:50] Maya: noted. item two: security and compliance docs. are SOC two artifacts ready for reviewers?

[07:05] Ravi: most are done; we still have the KMS/HSM key rotation proof that security wants. security is okay with the timeline but wants the rotation runbook finalized.

[07:25] Maya: action: Ravi to coordinate with security and deliver key rotation doc by Friday.

[07:40] Ravi: will do.

[07:50] Maya: item three: monitoring and dashboards — Connor, what's the ETA on the token-level cost dashboard?

[08:05] Connor: hooking up metrics this week, dashboards by thursday. i'll add example alerts for p95 latency and cost-per-1k-tokens. note: sample rate is 1/10 so might undercount short spikes.

[08:25] Elena: maybe add a synthetic test to detect KV cache regressions; if prefix caches stop warming we'll see latency spikes.

[08:40] Connor: good idea, synthetic bench every 15 minutes.

[08:55] Maya: item four: smoke tests and canary criteria. we need a checklist for canary: traffic ramp schedule, abort thresholds, fallback variant mapping, and runbook contact. Priya to compose the template?

[09:12] Priya: yes i'll draft the canary template and share by EOD Friday.

[09:25] Maya: on rollouts, we also decided earlier to have a staged ramp across regions to reduce blast radius. make sure capacity reservations for Dedicated are in place.

[09:40] Ravi: capacity is provisioned but not fully reserved for all customers; Ops needs final approval to lock it in.

[09:52] Elena: ops and billing need a final call out: reserved capacity pricing and burst policy. otherwise customers will be surprised when we throttle.

[10:05] Maya: add to launch comms.

[10:15] Speaker 6: quick question on the incident follow-ups, any outstanding customer postmortem items to share?

[10:28] Priya: we've reached out to affected customers, one escalation remains open but is on the customer success queue. not blocking.

[10:40] Ravi: also a note that our fallback mapping currently doesn't include an explicit region fallback; we should add region fallback in case of AZ level issues. that's an engineering addition but low effort.

[10:58] Elena: i'll add region fallback to the runtime routing tickets.

[11:10] Maya: great. near the end — who owns the final sign-off next week? we need an stakeholders list.

[11:22] Priya: sign-off: Maya (product), Ravi (eng), Connor (sre), Sarah (security). i will send the doc to Sarah and cc legal for release notes.

[11:40] Maya: ok recap and next steps: Priya to finalize checklist and canary template; Ravi to deliver key rotation doc; Connor to finish mitigation script and dashboards; Elena to move embeddings rerank to post-launch and add kernel guard; all to review perf plan and load test sheet. schedule follow-up sync next tuesday after load test.

[12:05] Ravi: one more thing, add regression validation for quantized models to the QA matrix.

[12:20] Maya: done. thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.

End transcript.
